beats.narration_en: At night, these lane lines seem to glow, lit only by your headlights.
Zoom in, and the paint is packed with thousands of tiny glass beads.
Light enters a bead, bounces off the back, and bends straight back the way it came.
Without those beads, that same paint looks dull and nearly vanishes at night.
That extra glow can buy a driver a crucial extra second to see the lane at night.
A tiny glass sphere, doing one precise job, on every striped road.
